newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Eight people killed in violence in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Eight people killed in violence in Karachi.

text.p: Gunmen killed at least four people and wounded 14 in an attack on the offices of a political party, taking the number of violent deaths here on Monday to eight, ambulance workers said.
Officials of the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) party said four attackers in a yellow vehicle had fired on their office in the Risala area of District South.
The death toll may well rise, the ambulance workers said.
Police confirmed a shooting incident had taken place, but gave no details. No group immediately claimed responsibility.
Earlier on Monday, at least four people, including a woman, were shot dead in separate incidents in District East, police said.
An unidentified woman was killed in Gulistan-e-Jauhar neighbourhood, a 25-year-old man in Korangi, a young man in Ibrahim Hyderi and an aged man in Steel Town.
There was no immediate word on the motives for the killings.

Violence in this southern port city has risen in recent weeks amid tension between the mainstream MQM, now part of a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, and the rival MQM-Haqiqi splinter group.
Unidentified gunmen killed two MQM-Haqiqi militants in an attack on the party's headquarters, known locally as the White House, in the Landhi district on Thursday.
About 75 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
